Parting Shot preserves Incineroar for a later Intimidate pivot while bringing in Kingambit against a weakened Garchomp at -2 Attack, with Supreme Overlord giving Kingambit a boost from the earlier Azumarill faint. That seems like the better line, so I'll go with Parting Shot.

decisions.hidden_reasoning:
I'm tracking Kingambit's current Attack stage at +1 after Swords Dance and Incineroar's Intimidate, with Supreme Overlord boosting its power by 20% from two fainted allies.

Incineroar is at 22% HP (~44) and isn't the one that Mega Evolved—that was Garchomp. Checking type matchups, Kingambit's main moves (Kowtow Cleave, Iron Head, Sucker Punch) are all resisted or neutral against Incineroar's Fire/Dark typing, while Incineroar's Flare Blitz hits Kingambit for super effective damage since Fire beats Steel, making this exchange riskier than it first appeared.

Plugging in the adjusted power with resist applied, I land around 60-70 damage after the random roll, still not enough to KO but a solid chunk given Incineroar's HP pool.

Thinking about speed order: Kingambit is slower, so Incineroar acts first. If it attacks, Sucker Punch gets priority and hits before Incineroar's move connects, likely securing the KO; but if Incineroar uses Parting Shot or another status move instead, Sucker Punch would whiff since it only works against attacking moves. Kowtow Cleave stays reliable regardless of what Incineroar does.

Incineroar's been toggling between Taunt and Parting Shot, so it'll likely repeat Parting Shot or go for Flare Blitz. Sucker punch wins if it attacks, Kowtow wins if it doesn't — but if it uses Parting Shot to switch out, I need to consider whether Kowtow then hits the incoming switch-in instead.

Since Kowtow would hit the new target either way while sucker punch would fail against a switch, Kowtow is the safer choice overall. I'll go with Kowtow Cleave.
